question: Explain why polarisation proves the transverse nature of light waves.

options.A: Polarisation proves light is longitudinal because longitudinal vibrations can be restricted to one plane.
options.B: Polarisation restricts light vibrations to one direction perpendicular to propagation. Only transverse waves have vibrations in different transverse directions that can be restricted; longitudinal waves vibrate along propagation and cannot be polarised. Since light can be polarised, it is transverse.
options.C: Polarisation proves light is transverse because the wavelength of light is very small.
options.D: All waves, including longitudinal sound waves, can be polarised, so polarisation does not identify wave type.
